blocks.text: Forsskål, in Descriptio Animalium, p. 9, also lists the turtur [turtledove] among the migratory birds of Alexandria that arrive with the flooding of the Nile (that is, either toward the end of April or at the beginning of May). But he wrongly wrote the name of the animal as كمري [kmry] for قمري [qumrī]; see Golius, Lexic. Arab. p. 1964, whose feminine is قُمْرِيَّة [qumriyya]; the male is also called ساق حرّ [sāq ḥurr], on which see Bochart, preceding Chapter, p. 52, marginal note. By a strange error Hufnagel, V. S. V., in the Annotatt. in Cantic. in the Repertorium für biblische und morgenl. Litterat. vol. 10, p. 243 [II, 598] 243, note b), confuses the turtur [turtledove] with the turdus [thrush], Arab. سمرمر [smrmr], which Forsskål, p. 6 of the book cited, says arrives at Aleppo in the months of July and August. But there is no one who does not know that the turdus [thrush] is of an entirely different kind from the turtur [turtledove].
